# Architecture Overview How mdNinja is put together, and why each piece exists. ## 1. The Living Canon Principle Git repositories are the source of truth. The operating model: 1. **Markdown on disk is the database.** ADRs, roadmaps, and diagrams are files under `mdninja/`; there is no parallel store to keep in sync. 2. **Edits are filesystem writes.** The workbench saves with `fs.writeFile`; Git status, diffs, and commits stay native. 3. **Agents operate through canon.** AI assistants read and write the same files through the MCP server, under the rules encoded in each ADR's `🤖 Agent Enforcement` section. 4. **Dual equal panels.** Split view gives two fully-capable panels; there is no primary/context panel distinction. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Repo["Git repository"] CANON["mdninja/ canon"] DOCS["docs/ user docs"] CODE["source code"] end CLI["@mdninja/cli
(dev · init · mcp)"] WEB["@mdninja/web
(Next.js workbench)"] AGENTS["AI assistants
(MCP over stdio)"] CLI --> Repo WEB --> Repo AGENTS --> Repo ``` ## 2. Monorepo Layout | Path | Owns | | :--- | :--- | | `apps/web` | The workbench: Next.js 15 App Router frontend, filesystem API routes, and the canon bundler (`scripts/sync-canon.mjs`). | | `apps/web/src-tauri` | Tauri 2 crate wrapping the same web frontend for native desktop. | | `packages/cli` | `@mdninja/cli`: `dev` (static-server workbench launcher), `init` (scaffold), `mcp` (stdio MCP server). | | `packages/canon` | `@mdninja/canon` — the single contract for `.mdninja/config.json` shape and the canonical `mdninja/` layout. Consumed by the CLI and the web scaffold route alike, so the two can never drift. | The web app is one deployable; the CLI is one npm package; the canonical layout is one package. Three artifacts, one contract. ## 3. The AST Pipeline Documents render through [unified](https://github.com/unifiedjs/unified): ``` remark-parse → remark-gfm → remark-math → remark-rehype → rehype-katex → rehype-highlight → rehype-stringify ``` * `remark-gfm` brings tables, task lists, strikethrough, and autolinks. * `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` render `$inline$` and `$$block$$` LaTeX with zero layout shift. * `rehype-highlight` colors fenced code blocks; the palette is fixed dark in both light and dark modes (see [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for the rationale). Mermaid fenced blocks are split out *before* the pipeline — they never pass through remark as code, they become `` segments. ## 4. Diagram Engine `MermaidViewer` renders intercepted `` ```mermaid `` blocks into SVG: * **Standalone documents** (file is only a diagram) fill 100% panel height with a pan/zoom viewport (`react-zoom-pan-pinch`, 60fps) and an icon-only zoom cluster. * **Embedded diagrams** render at natural aspect ratio inline with the text. * **Theming is derived, never configured.** Every Mermaid `themeVariables` color resolves from the live CSS custom properties (`--bg-*`, `--text-*`, `--accent*`, `--border-*`) at render time; a `MutationObserver` on `` re-renders on dark/light, reading-palette, or accent changes. There is no separate diagram theme (ADR 0010). * Diagram surfaces are read-only; source edits go through the panel toolbar. ## 5. API Surface | Route | Method | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `/api/files` | GET | Full repository scan: canon tree, `docs/`, `.agents/`, root Markdown, with document sizes. | | `/api/content` | GET / POST | Read one document / write one document. Read falls back to the bundled canon snapshot when the file isn't on disk (serverless deployments). Writes are path-validated against the project root. | | `/api/scaffold` | POST | Initialize the canon. Delegates to `@mdninja/canon` so CLI and web scaffolds are byte-identical. | | `/api/auth/github` | GET | Start OAuth: binds a CSRF `state` to the browser via an `mdninja_oauth_state` httpOnly cookie, then redirects to GitHub. | | `/api/auth/callback/github` | GET | Verify `state` against the cookie, exchange the code ephemerally, `postMessage` the account payload to the opener window, and retain nothing on the server (ADR 0004). | ## 6. Data Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant UI as Workbench UI participant API as Next.js API routes participant FS as Filesystem (Git repo) UI->>API: GET /api/files API->>FS: scan (canon, docs, .agents, root) FS-->>UI: repository tree UI->>API: GET /api/content?path=roadmaps/roadmap.md API->>FS: readFile (fallback: bundled canon snapshot) FS-->>UI: markdown UI->>UI: unified pipeline renders UI->>API: POST /api/content {path, content} API->>FS: writeFile (path-validated) Note over FS: git status shows the change ``` ## 7. Deployment Models * **Local / CLI** — `mdninja dev` serves the workbench bound to the live filesystem; everything reads and writes the real repo. * **Serverless (Vercel, production)** — root files live outside the function bundle root, so at build time `sync-canon` snapshots the canon into `apps/web/src/lib/canon-data.json` (and `public/schema.json` from `@mdninja/canon`). `/api/content` and `/api/files` fall back to that snapshot when the path isn't on disk (ADR 0005). Edits remain disk-backed on any filesystem-deploy host. * **Desktop (Tauri 2)** — the Tauri crate loads the same build; `tauri dev` hot-reloads against the dev server, packaged builds load the static frontend (ADR 0008). ## 8. Multi-User Isolation A public deployment like `mdninja.navinhill.com` serves everyone the same read surface; any visitor can then connect their own GitHub account: * The OAuth exchange is **ephemeral** — tokens only ever transit the callback route in memory. * Accounts, tokens, and repo lists persist **only in the visitor's browser `localStorage`.** * The server stores nothing per-user: zero accounts, zero tokens, zero private-repo metadata (ADR 0004). ## 9. MCP & CLI `@mdninja/cli` ships three entry points (full reference in [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md)): * `dev` — serve the visual workbench for any directory (`-p`, `-d`, `--no-open`). * `init` — scaffold `.mdninja/config.json` + the canonical `mdninja/` layout via `@mdninja/canon`. * `mcp` — stdio MCP server exposing `get_canon_structure`, `read_canon_doc`, `write_canon_doc`, `list_adrs`, `create_adr`, `get_roadmap`, `update_roadmap_task` (ADR 0007). The `create_adr` tool enforces sequential numbering and the `🤖 Agent Enforcement` section. ## 10. Decisions Index | ADR | Subject | | :--- | :--- | | [0001](../mdninja/decisions/0001-monorepo-structure.md) | Monorepo structure | | [0002](../mdninja/decisions/0002-zero-constraint-split-panel.md) | Zero-constraint split panels | | [0003](../mdninja/decisions/0003-latex-katex-integration.md) | KaTeX math integration | | [0004](../mdninja/decisions/0004-zero-leak-multi-user-isolation.md) | Zero-leak multi-user isolation | | [0005](../mdninja/decisions/0005-bundled-canon-fallback.md) | Bundled canon fallback | | [0006](../mdninja/decisions/0006-rebrand-and-dynamic-canon.md) | Rebrand + dynamic canon discovery | | [0007](../mdninja/decisions/0007-mcp-server-and-cli-architecture.md) | MCP server & CLI architecture | | [0008](../mdninja/decisions/0008-tauri-desktop-integration.md) | Tauri desktop integration | | [0009](../mdninja/decisions/0009-ui-overhaul-and-github-oauth.md) | UI overhaul & GitHub OAuth | | [0010](../mdninja/decisions/0010-diagram-theme-derivation-and-edit-consolidation.md) | Diagram theme derivation & edit consolidation |

# CLI & MCP Reference

`@mdninja/cli` is a zero-dependency-to-run launcher. `npx` fetches it on demand; nothing is installed globally.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dev` (default) | Serve the visual workbench for the target directory. |
| `init` | Scaffold `.mdninja/config.json` + the canonical `mdninja/` layout. |
| `mcp` | Run the Model Context Protocol server over `stdio`. |
| `build` | Re-sync the bundled canon and build the production web bundle (monorepo only). |

### `dev` options

| Flag | Default | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-p, --port <n>` | `3000` | Listening port. |
| `-d, --dir <path>` | current directory | Target repo to scan and serve. |
| `--no-open` | (opens) | Skip auto-opening the browser. |

Example:

```bash
npx @mdninja/cli dev -p 8080 -d ../other-repo --no-open
```

### `init` options

| Flag | Default | Behavior |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `-d, --dir <path>` | current directory | Where to scaffold. |
| `-f, --force` | off | Overwrite an existing `.mdninja/config.json`. |

`init` writes exactly the fields the runtime reads (see [configuration guide](configuration-guide.md)): `$schema`, `name`, `canon`.

### `build`

Runs `sync-canon` then `next build` inside the mdNinja monorepo. It is a convenience for maintainers of **this** repo, intended to work from the installed package location. In a different repository use the monorepo's own `npm run build`.

## MCP Server

The `mcp` command speaks MCP over `stdio`, so any MCP-capable assistant can read and write your living canon without you copy-pasting paths.

### Wire it up

Claude Desktop (`claude_desktop_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mdninja": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mdninja/cli", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor / Windsurf / other: add a stdio server with the same command and args.

### Tools

| Tool | Arguments | Output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `get_canon_structure` | — | Full hierarchy + metadata of the canon. |
| `read_canon_doc` | `filePath` | Markdown content of one document. |
| `write_canon_doc` | `filePath`, `content` | Writes the document, creating parent folders as needed. |
| `list_adrs` | — | Every ADR with number, title, status. |
| `create_adr` | `title`, `context`, `decision` (+ optional `status`, `consequences`, `enforcement`) | A new, sequentially-numbered ADR with a `🤖 Agent Enforcement` section. |
| `get_roadmap` | — | Parsed tasks and checklists from the roadmap. |
| `update_roadmap_task` | `taskQuery`, `completed` | Toggles the matching task between `[ ]` and `[x]`. |

All paths are relative to the root of the directory the server was started from.

# Configuration

mdNinja separates **tool configuration** (hidden, machine-read) from **repository documentation** (visible, human-read). Three surfaces cover it: a project config file, environment variables, and browser-side user preferences.

## 1. `.mdninja/config.json`

Lives at your project root. The single source of truth for its shape is [`packages/canon/index.js`](../packages/canon/index.js) (`@mdninja/canon`) — both `mdninja init` and the in-app scaffold route write the identical artifact, and the runtime reads exactly what's below.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://mdninja.navinhill.com/schema.json",
  "name": "My Project",
  "canon": "./mdninja"
}
```

| Field | Default | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `name` | folder name | Display name in the sidebar project picker. |
| `canon` | `./mdninja` | Relative path to the living-canon folder. |

Scanning is directory-based over the canon folder, `docs/`, `.agents/`, and root Markdown. If `docs/` doesn't exist in your repo, it won't appear in the tree.

## 2. Environment variables

Used when self-hosting the web deployment (Vercel or a local server). Copy from [`.env.example`](../.env.example).

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | production | `http://localhost:3000` | Canonical app origin. Must byte-for-byte match the origin registered on your GitHub OAuth App, because the callback URL derives from it. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` | for GitHub connect | `""` | GitHub OAuth App client ID. |
| `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` | for GitHub connect | `""` | GitHub OAuth App client secret. |

GitHub is the only optional feature that needs env config; the rest of the app runs with zero environment.

With `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` left at its localhost default, connect-a-repo simply won't fire — there's no registered callback to redirect to.

## 3. GitHub OAuth App setup

1. GitHub → **Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App**.
2. Application name: anything you like. Homepage URL: your app origin (e.g. `https://mdninja.navinhill.com`).
3. Authorization callback URL: `<your origin>/api/auth/callback/github`.
4. Generate the client secret, then set `GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` and `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET` in your Vercel project (or `.env.local` for local serving).

Token flow: the callback route performs the code exchange, hands the account to your browser via `postMessage`, and retains nothing. Tokens, profiles, and repo lists live in your browser's `localStorage`. See [ADR 0004](../mdninja/decisions/0004-zero-leak-multi-user-isolation.md).

## 4. Browser-side user preferences

Settings → **Styling, Themes & Comfort** holds the reading experience: reading palette, accent color, font family/size, line height, document max width, and the folder icon engine. These are per-visitor UI state — they never touch your repo.

# Contributing

This repo holds the product, its living canon, and its agent operating rules in one place. The rules below are the contract for humans and AI agents alike — `AGENTS.md` at the root is the executable version for agents.

## Commands

```bash
npm run dev        # web workbench on :3000
npm run build      # prebuild syncs the canon bundle, then next build
npm run lint       # next lint in apps/web
npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json   # typecheck
```

`npm run build` is the gate. It runs `prebuild` → `sync-canon` (regenerates `apps/web/src/lib/canon-data.json` from the repo's Markdown + `public/schema.json` from `@mdninja/canon`) → `next build` (which also typechecks). If you edited canon docs, the build is what ships them into the bundle — a stale `canon-data.json` means a stale demo.

For the monorepo's desktop target: `cargo check --manifest-path apps/web/src-tauri/Cargo.toml` validates the Rust crate.

## What CI runs

`.github/workflows/release.yml` fires on `v*` tags: `npm ci` → `sync-canon` → `build` → `mdninja --help` / `--version` smoke → publish `@mdninja/cli` to npm with provenance → GitHub release. There is no PR-time check pipeline, so **run the build locally before pushing.**

## Repo layout

| Path | Owns |
| :--- | :--- |
| `apps/web` | Next.js workbench (`src/`) + canon bundler (`scripts/sync-canon.mjs`) |
| `apps/web/src-tauri` | Tauri crate (native shell around the same web build) |
| `packages/cli` | `@mdninja/cli` — dev server, scaffold, and stdio MCP server |
| `packages/canon` | Single source of truth for the `.mdninja/config.json` contract + canon layout |
| `mdninja/` | This project's own living canon (ADRs, roadmaps, changelog, audits, research) |
| `docs/` | User-facing documentation |
| `.agents/skills` | Executable agent workflow skills |

## Rules that matter

1. **Canon before code, canon with code.** New architecture → ADR in `mdninja/decisions/` (template: `0000-template.md`, must include a `🤖 Agent Enforcement` section). Multi-step work → roadmap entry first. Behavior or plan changes → `[Unreleased]` changelog entry in the same session.
2. **Docs verified the session they're written.** Every command, flag, and path in `docs/` must actually run. A documented flag the code doesn't have is a bug.
3. **No dead UI, no dead config.** A control that doesn't connect to state, or a config field nothing reads, gets deleted. Advertised capability must be implemented capability.
4. **Session closeout.** Changelog → docs accuracy pass → commit + push. A dirty working tree at session end is an unfinished task.
5. **Doc voice.** State what exists and why, in one beat. No "it's not X, it's Y", no filler, no negative-space descriptions ("this doesn't do…").

## Style

* TypeScript strict mode in `apps/web`; keep imports explicit, components small, and CSS variables as the only theme tokens (see `mdninja/standards/coding-standards.md`).
* Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `refactor:`, `chore:` + scope.
* Markdown over database. If a note needs to survive the session, it goes in `mdninja/`, not in an agent's memory.

# Getting Started

mdNinja is a visual workbench for the living canon — your project's ADRs, roadmaps, diagrams, and notes as one navigable reading surface. This page gets you running; the [user guide](user-guide.md) covers what to do once it's open.

## Run it

Pick the path that fits:

### Option A — Any repo, zero clone (recommended)

```bash
npx @mdninja/cli            # serve the current directory
npx @mdninja/cli -d /path/to/repo
npx @mdninja/cli init       # scaffold a fresh living canon in this repo
```

The workbench, MCP server, and scaffolder all operate on the directory you point at (`-d` or cwd).

### Option B — Live demo

[mdninja.navinhill.com](https://mdninja.navinhill.com) runs this exact repository's canon. Zero install, good for a first look.

### Option C — This monorepo, locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jamesnavinhill/mdninja.git
cd mdninja
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. Edits write straight to disk; Git shows them as normal working-tree changes.

### Option D — Desktop (Tauri)

```bash
cd apps/web
npm run tauri dev
```

Develops the same Next.js frontend inside a native webview. Requires a Rust toolchain, since Tauri compiles a small Rust binary around it. No installer is shipped yet — desktop build tooling exists, packaging is a roadmap item.

## What you'll see

* **Icon rail** (far left): jump to a canon section, toggle dark/light, open Settings.
* **File tree**: the repository's canon, `docs/`, `.agents/`, and root Markdown.
* **Panel(s)**: rendered Markdown. `Cmd/Ctrl + \` splits into two equal panels.

Keyboard map:

| Shortcut | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Cmd + \` / `Ctrl + \` | Toggle equal-split panels |
| `Cmd + B` / `Ctrl + B` | Toggle file tree sidebar |
| `Cmd + S` / `Ctrl + S` | Save the active document to disk |

## Where things live

| Folder | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mdninja/decisions/` | ADRs with agent-enforcement rules |
| `mdninja/roadmaps/` | Living timelines and task checklists |
| `mdninja/diagrams/` | Mermaid maps (render with 60fps pan/zoom) |

| `mdninja/standards/` | Coding and UI conventions |
| `docs/` | This documentation |
| `.agents/` | Agent skills and directives |

# Troubleshooting

Fast fixes for the failures you'll actually hit.

## Workbench won't start

| Symptom | Fix |
| :--- | :--- |
| `EADDRINUSE` on the port | Something already owns it: `npx @mdninja/cli -p 3001`, or kill the old process. |
| Page loads, file tree is empty | The target directory has no Markdown the scanner reads. Run `npx @mdninja/cli init` to scaffold a canon, or point `-d` at a repo that has one. |
| `mdninja build` in a foreign repo | `build` targets the mdNinja monorepo. Use it there; elsewhere use `dev` — the workbench works on any repo. |

## GitHub "Connect Account" does nothing

The OAuth popup needs a registered callback that matches your app's origin exactly, character for character:

1. `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` must equal the origin the OAuth App knows (apex domain, no trailing slash drift).
2. The OAuth App's **Authorization callback URL** must be `<that origin>/api/auth/callback/github`.
3. Local dev: register `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/github` on the OAuth App, and keep `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` at its default while you test locally.

If the popup opens GitHub and returns an error page, the origin mismatch is the cause — the exchange is ephemeral, so there's no server log to dig through.

## Diagram renders blank

Mermaid measures text to size its canvas. In some headless/automated browser contexts that measurement comes back zero-width, and the gantt renders empty. It renders correctly in a normal desktop browser. If you see a blank diagram:

1. Confirm the fenced block says ```` ```mermaid ```` (a stray character in the fence breaks interception).
2. Validate the syntax against the [Mermaid Live Editor](https://mermaid.live) — the app surfaces the render error message in place of the SVG when the source is invalid.
3. Hard-refresh; a stale bundle from before a theme change occasionally shows a stale (or blank first) paint.

## Code blocks look "wrong" in light theme

Deliberate: fenced code stays dark in both modes so snippets read the same regardless of palette. The policy lives in `apps/web/src/styles/markdown.css` (`--code-block-bg`). Inline `code` follows the theme.

## Docs look stale on the hosted demo

The web bundle ships a build-time snapshot of the canon (`apps/web/src/lib/canon-data.json`, regenerated by `sync-canon` on every `npm run build`). A docs-only push needs a rebuild+deploy to show up on Vercel; the local workbench always reads the disk live.

## Desktop build fails

* `cargo` missing → install the Rust toolchain (`rustup`).
* Windows without WebView2 → the OS webview prerequisite; Tauri's build output tells you which one is missing.
* Port clash with a running `npm run dev` → `tauri dev` starts the web build on `:3000` via `beforeDevCommand`; stop the other one first.

# User Guide

How to drive the workbench once it's open.

## The layout

```
┌──────┬──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Rail │ File tree    │ Panel(s)                                  │
│      │              │ ┌ toolbar: breadcrumb · save · edit · ┐   │
│ canon│ mdninja/     │ │ split                                │   │
│ docs │   decisions  │ ├──────────────────────────────────────┤   │
│ .agents│  roadmaps  │ │ rendered markdown / raw editor       │   │
│ root │   diagrams   │ │                                        │   │
│      │ docs/        │ └────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
└──────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

* **Rail** — jump straight to a canon section (decisions, roadmaps, …), `☀/☾` flips dark/light, the avatar opens Settings.
* **File tree** — everything the scanner found: canon, `docs/`, `.agents/`, root Markdown. Click a folder to collapse, a file to open it in the active panel.
* **Panels** — the reading surface. Single panel by default; `Cmd/Ctrl + \` splits into two equal panels with a draggable divider. Each panel has its own toolbar.

## Reading a document

Files render as Markdown with tables, task lists, KaTeX math, and highlighted code blocks. Markdown links to other repo files open inside the workbench instead of navigating away.

## Diagrams

Fenced `` ```mermaid `` blocks render as interactive vectors:

* Scroll to zoom, drag to pan. The floating buttons (bottom-right) are zoom in / out / reset.
* A file that is *only* a diagram fills the full panel height.
* Diagrams take their colors from your active theme, palette, and accent automatically.
* To edit a diagram's source, flip the panel into edit mode (toolbar) — the raw Markdown is there.

Diagram syntax is standard [Mermaid](https://mermaid.js.org/).

## Editing and saving

* Toolbar **edit** icon (or the same button showing a "preview" icon while editing) flips the panel between rendered preview and raw Markdown.
* Type, then press `Cmd/Ctrl + S` or click Save. The write goes straight to the filesystem — Git picks it up from there.
* The save pill tells you the state: `saved` fades on its own, `unsaved` means there's work to persist.

## Themes and comfort

Settings → **Styling, Themes & Comfort**:

* **Reading palettes** — Default, Tokyo Night, Nord Frost, GitHub Dimmed, Paper Sepia. Each works in both dark and light.
* **Accent color** — full spectrum picker; diagrams, links, and UI chrome follow it live.
* **Typography** — font family, size, line height, and document max-width sliders apply instantly.
* **Icon engine** — switch the folder icons to Lucide or Phosphor and override the icon for individual canon sections.

Dark/light is the rail toggle; palette and accent are the Settings job. Everything re-renders live.

## Connect a GitHub repo

Settings → **GitHub Connections** → *Add Account* opens the OAuth popup. Your repositories load into the panel; connect as many accounts as you like.

Security model: the token exchange is ephemeral on the server, and tokens live only in your browser's `localStorage`. Nothing account-related is ever stored on the server (see [ADR 0004](../mdninja/decisions/0004-zero-leak-multi-user-isolation.md)).

## Daily workflow, condensed

1. Open the repo's canon (icon rail → `roadmaps` is a good start).
2. Read the ADR that governs the work you're doing.
3. Split (`Cmd + \`) when comparing two docs side by side.
4. Edit → `Cmd + S` → commit with your normal Git flow.

---
name: untard
description: "Use when: a constraint, process, abstraction, gate, dependency, daemon, or risk-surface is slowing work down and you suspect it earns less than it costs. Trigger to put a thing on trial for its right to exist and rip out net-negative drag. The complement to /upstream — upstream fixes the source of a problem; untard deletes the thing that should never have been a problem."
argument-hint: "the constraint / process / abstraction / risk-surface to put on trial"
---

# Untard

> Untard asks *should this thing exist at all, and is it paying rent?* If it's net-negative drag,
> you don't optimize it — you delete it.

## Purpose

Catch and remove **development-retarding drag**: constraints, gates, abstractions, daemons, shims,
profiles, or risk-surfaces that cost more than they return. Every constraint we accept is a tax. The
tax is only worth paying if the **net benefit is clearly in our favor**. If it isn't, the thing is
slowing us down for nothing — un-tard it.

## The one question

**"Is this thing's net benefit in our favor — or is it just retarding development?"**

If you can't state a concrete benefit that outweighs its cost + risk surface, the default verdict is
**remove**.

## The boogeyman test — the self-imposed constraint

Before you accept a "we have to," find out who is holding the gun. **A constraint you created is not
a law. It is a boogeyman** — it only has power while you believe it came from outside.

Walk it: *"what forces this?"* → answer → *"is THAT in our control?"* → repeat. In a one-dev +
agents shop, almost every "hard constraint" turns out to be a setting, a default, a convention, or a
hack papering over a collision of two of your *own* choices. Keep walking until you hit something
genuinely outside your control — a protocol, a vendor API, physics. Everything above that line is
negotiable. So renegotiate it.

If the only thing forcing the pain is something *you* set: stop obeying it. We do it our way.

## The procedure

1. **Name the thing on trial.** The exact constraint / process / abstraction / risk-surface, in one
   sentence. (e.g. "a second Multica daemon under a different profile.")
2. **Tally the cost.** What does it cost us *continuously*? Drag, ceremony, a second moving part, a
   nondeterminism, a collision/injection surface, cognitive load, one more thing that can break.
3. **Tally the benefit.** What does it actually buy us — concretely, today, for THIS project (one dev
   + agents, greenfield)? Not in theory, not "best practice," not "an enterprise would."
4. **Net it out.** Benefit minus cost-and-risk. If it isn't *clearly* positive, it's dead weight.
5. **Rip it out at the root**, then `/upstream` the hole it leaves so nothing downstream re-grows it.
   If it IS net-positive, say why in one line and keep it — don't torch working hygiene out of zeal.

## Hard signals you're looking at tardation

- A second moving part that does what one already does (a redundant daemon / profile / service / gate).
- Ceremony justified only by "best practice" or "an enterprise would" — not by THIS product's need.
- A risk surface (nondeterminism, collision, injection point) accepted with **no** benefit that beats it.
- Something everyone routes *around* instead of *through* — that's the tell it shouldn't be there.
- A constraint that only made sense for a stage we've already left.

## Anti-patterns (don't be the tard)

- Keeping a thing because it's already there (sunk cost), or because removing it is mildly scary.
- Swinging to the opposite extreme. Untard removes *net-negative* drag; it does **not** ban all
  hygiene, lints, or pre-commit checks that cheaply catch drift. Aim for the middle, then adjust on
  results. (A test that freezes a transient shape = tard. A format check that catches drift before
  commit = rent-paying — keep it.)
- Deleting something you never actually netted out. Do the tally, *then* cut.

## Relationship to /upstream

- `/upstream`: a problem exists → trace to source → fix it THERE.
- `/untard`: a *thing* exists → does it deserve to → if not, DELETE it, then upstream the gap.
- Run them as a pair: untard removes the net-negative thing; upstream solves the reason it was there
  so it can't grow back.

## Field receipt — the boogeyman symlink

Seven product repos each carried a `docs/_standards/` **symlink** into the shared `_ops` standards
canon, backed by a gate that wanted that file *present*. It looked load-bearing. It was pure
net-negative drag: the symlink only resolved in the nested-local layout and died everywhere that
counts — standalone clone, CI, isolated workdir — and it pointed at a path that had since been
renamed, so it was **dead on arrival in all seven**.

The "constraint" forcing it — *"a repo must reach the shared canon from inside itself"* — was a
boogeyman. It was born from trying to have it both ways: standalone repos that secretly depend on a
parent file. Net it out: cost = a brittle, dead, layout-coupled link in seven places; benefit =
none. **Verdict: cut.**

Upstream fix (the duality worth burning in): **repos go lean and self-sufficient** — they reference
the canon by *identity*, never require the file present, never carry a copy — **while `_ops` stays
the unbounded single source**, the brain that holds the full text. Risk drops exponentially (no
cross-repo file coupling left to break) and nothing duplicates (no drift). The repo *names* the rule;
`_ops` *owns* the rule.

Lesson: when you catch yourself building a bridge so A can reach B, first ask whether A should depend
on B at all. The bridge is usually the tell that the dependency itself is wrong.

---
name: upstream
description: "Use when: an error, constraint, failure, surprise, or hard decision appears - or when work is drifting toward patching symptoms. Trigger to course-correct by tracing a problem to its source before fixing it. Catch-all for 'why does this keep happening', repeated failures across places, brittle workarounds, or 'should we patch or fix properly'."
argument-hint: "the error, constraint, or decision to trace"
---

# Upstream

## Purpose

Trace any problem to its true source and fix it THERE, instead of patching the hole, bucket-catching
the overflow, or hand-rolling the boulder out of the stream. If upstream is in shape, everything
downstream flows. This is the single most important rule for every agent and repo in the family.

## The procedure

1. **Ask the first question.** "Why does this exist in the first place?" Not "how do I get past it" -
   "why is it here at all."
2. **Walk upstream.** Take the answer and ask why again. Repeat, noticing the surroundings (the
   connected decisions, contracts, and assumptions) as you go.
3. **Stop at the source.** Keep going until the answer is no longer within our control - you have
   reached a core primitive, contract, or external dependency. That point is the source.
4. **Decide at the source, not before.** Only once you can see the full system, the connected
   decisions, and the direct and indirect effects do you choose a deep fix vs a tactical one. Pick the
   most proportionate fix at the source - do not overengineer, do not underfix.
5. **Fix it there, once.** Remove the cause. Then everything downstream of it flows without per-case
   handling.

## Hard signals you are NOT at the source yet

- The same symptom shows up in more than one place. Two+ instances of one failure = proof of a single
  upstream constraint. Fix that one source; do NOT chase the instances one domino at a time.
- Your fix tolerates, skips, retries, or works-around the symptom rather than removing its cause.
- Your fix only holds for the exact environment you are in (breaks in CI, a fresh clone, an isolated
  workdir, another repo) - that means you patched a layout/assumption, not the source.

## Anti-patterns (forbidden)

- Patching the hole / bucket-catching the overflow / hand-rolling the boulder out of the stream.
- Adding a tolerance flag, conditional skip, retry, or shim to make a symptom pass.
- Building broad compatibility layers to absorb an upstream that simply is not in shape.

## Corollary: downstream never depends on upstream's physical presence

A downstream gate or consumer must validate only its OWN artifacts. It must never require an
upstream-owned file to be physically present (e.g. via a layout-dependent symlink). Reference upstream
by its canonical identity, not by mounting it. "Upstream it" - canon to the single source, organize by
concern, and let downstream flow from it.

## Worked example

`docs:check` failed in Multica workdirs because it required `docs/_standards/dev-docs-standard.md`,
reachable only through a relative symlink to the `_ops` repo. Symptom appeared in two repos.
- Patch (wrong): tolerate the missing symlink / skip the entry when absent.
- Source (right): a downstream gate was requiring an upstream-owned file's physical presence. Removed
  that requirement from both gates so each validates only its own docs. The symlink stays as a dev
  convenience nothing gates on. One source fix, both instances gone, holds in every checkout.

## Output

State the why-chain explicitly (each "why" and its answer), name the source, name the proportionate
fix at the source, and confirm the downstream cases now flow without per-case handling.

# Project Agents Operational Directive

This document defines operational rules, personas, and behavioral constraints for all AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code, Windsurf, Roo Code, Gemini) working in this repository.

## 1. The Living Canon Mandate
* All architectural choices must be formalized in `mdninja/decisions/` using the standard ADR format (`0000-template.md`).
* When planning multi-step features, read `mdninja/roadmaps/roadmap.md` first to align with current phase priorities.
* Do not introduce external database dependencies for documentation; all persistent operational context must reside as Markdown in `mdninja/`.

## 2. Directory Layout
* `mdninja/decisions/`: Immutable decision records.
* `mdninja/roadmaps/`: Living execution timeline and checklists.
* `mdninja/diagrams/`: Mermaid and Excalidraw visual maps.
* `docs/`: User-facing and API documentation.
* `.agents/skills/`: Executable workflow instructions.

## 3. Agent Rules of Engagement
* **DO:** Check off completed tasks in `mdninja/roadmaps/roadmap.md` with `[x]` after verifying implementation.
* **DO:** Include the `🤖 Agent Enforcement` section in every new ADR.
* **DO:** Use the native Model Context Protocol (MCP) server (`mdninja mcp`) or tools for path-safe living canon reads, edits, and ADR scaffolding.
* **DO:** Run the production build (`npm run build`) after any code change and fix what breaks before ending the session.
* **DO NOT:** Commit `.next/` or build artifacts to Git.

## 4. Session Closeout (mandatory)
Every session ends with these steps, in order:

1. **Changelog entry.** If the session touched code, changed system behavior, or altered any plan (roadmap, ADR status, scope), add an entry under `[Unreleased]` in `mdninja/changelog/changelog.md`. Code edits without a changelog entry are an incomplete task.
2. **Docs accuracy pass.** Verify any documentation the session's changes affected (`docs/`, `README.md`, ADRs, roadmaps) still matches the code. Docs lie only when nobody checks.
3. **Commit and push.** Commit all work with a conventional commit message (`feat:`/`fix:`/`docs:`/`refactor:`/`chore:` + scope), then push to `origin` on the current branch. Work that lives only in a dirty working tree is unfinished work.

## 5. Documentation Voice
Docs are written for a human who will act on them, not for a model to sound good.
* **SAY THE THING.** "We do X." — stop. Never "we don't do Y, we do X" or "it's not Y, it's X." State what exists and why in one beat.
* **No filler.** Cut "in order to" chains, passive constructions, and throat-clearing preludes. If a sentence could be deleted without losing meaning, delete it.
* **Accurate by construction.** Every command, path, flag, and behavior written in a doc must be verified against the code in the same session it's written. A documented command that doesn't run is a defect, filed the same as a bug.
* **To the point, and only that.** One doc, one job. Cross-reference instead of repeating.

# mdNinja 🥷

> **The Zero-Constraint Living Canon Workbench & Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for Engineering Teams and AI Agents.**

[![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-15.5-black?style=flat-square&logo=next.js)](https://nextjs.org/)
[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.7-blue?style=flat-square&logo=typescript)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
[![Tauri 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tauri-2.0-orange?style=flat-square&logo=tauri)](https://tauri.app/)
[![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Protocol-purple?style=flat-square)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![Live Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_Demo-mdninja.navinhill.com-indigo?style=flat-square)](https://mdninja.navinhill.com)

**mdNinja** connects your engineering repository's Markdown documents—architecture blueprints, living roadmaps, ADRs, interactive diagrams, and AI agent memory—into an uncluttered, high-performance visual workbench and standardized MCP interface with **zero database silos**.

Explore the public live demo: **[mdninja.navinhill.com](https://mdninja.navinhill.com)**

---

## ⚡ Highlights

* **Zero-Constraint Equal Split Workspace:** Dual equal panels (`Cmd + \`) powered by `react-resizable-panels`. No artificial "primary vs context" restrictions—both panels have 100% identical capabilities.
* **Native Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server:** Out-of-the-box stdio integration for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, and Google Antigravity to navigate, read, write, and index the Living Canon.
* **Native Desktop Shell (Tauri 2.0):** The same Next.js frontend runs in an OS-native webview via a small Rust crate (`apps/web/src-tauri`) — lightweight, with no Electron runtime footprint. Desktop packaging is a roadmap item.
* **LaTeX Formula Typography:** Synchronous, zero-layout-shift mathematical rendering via KaTeX (`$math$` and `$$math$$`).
* **Unconstrained Vector Diagrams:** Interactive Mermaid.js code blocks converted into 60fps pan/zoom vectors that automatically derive their colors from your workspace theme, reading palette, and accent.
* **Direct Local Filesystem I/O:** Edits write directly to disk (`fs.writeFile`) with zero lag. Your Git repository remains the single source of truth.
* **Native Living Canon Discovery:** Scans and organizes `mdninja/` (ADRs, roadmaps, diagrams, audits), `docs/`, `.agents/`, and root Markdown.
* **Zero-Leak Multi-User Isolation:** Ephemeral OAuth exchange with browser-local `localStorage` persistence. Zero tokens or user repositories on the server ([ADR 0004](mdninja/decisions/0004-zero-leak-multi-user-isolation.md)).

---

## 🚀 Quick Start

### 1. Instant CLI Runner (Zero-Install)
Run mdNinja in any repository or directory using `npx`:

```bash
# Run the workbench against the current directory
npx @mdninja/cli

# Or serve an arbitrary repo explicitly
npx @mdninja/cli --dir /path/to/any/repo

# Scaffold the .mdninja config + canonical mdninja/ folders in the current directory
npx @mdninja/cli init
```

> `mdninja dev` (the default command) serves the repo named by `--dir`/`-d` (or the current directory if omitted). The scanner honors the target directory, so the workbench, MCP, and scaffold all operate on the same repo.

### 2. Connect Your AI Assistant (MCP)
Add mdNinja to your AI coding assistant (Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf) via stdio:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mdninja": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@mdninja/cli", "mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### 3. Native Desktop App (Tauri 2.0)
Build and run the native desktop shell:

```bash
cd apps/web
npm run tauri dev
```

### 4. Run Monorepo Locally

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jamesnavinhill/mdNinja.git
cd mdNinja
npm install
npm run dev
```

Visit `http://localhost:3000` in your browser.

---

## 📁 The Living Canon Layout

```
[Repository Root]
├── .mdninja/                      <-- [Hidden] Tool Configuration & Mappings
│   └── config.json                 <-- name + canon path; contract in packages/canon
│
├── mdninja/                       <-- [Visible] The Living Canon ("The Goods")
│   ├── audits/                     <-- Performance benchmarks & security audits
│   ├── changelog/                  <-- Version history & release notes
│   ├── decisions/                  <-- Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) with agent enforcement
│   ├── diagrams/                   <-- System schemas & sequence diagrams (Mermaid)
│   ├── notes/                      <-- Engineering scratchpads & technical notes
│   ├── research/                   <-- Spikes, token economics, parser benchmarks
│   ├── roadmaps/                   <-- Living Gantt charts & milestone execution checklists
│   └── standards/                  <-- UI philosophy, code conventions & agent directives
│
├── docs/                           <-- Product & API documentation
├── .agents/                        <-- AI agent skills, directives & operational memory
└── README.md, AGENTS.md            <-- Root Markdown files
```

---

## 🛠️ CLI Commands (`@mdninja/cli`)

| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `mdninja dev [options]` | Start the local visual workbench (default command). Options: `-p, --port <port>`, `--no-open`, `-d, --dir <path>` (serve that repo's canon; defaults to the current directory). |
| `mdninja init [options]` | Scaffold `.mdninja/config.json` and canonical directories (`mdninja/`). Options: `-f, --force`, `-d, --dir <path>`. |
| `mdninja mcp` | Launch the Model Context Protocol (MCP) server over `stdio` for AI assistants. |
| `mdninja build` | Sync living canon + build. **Requires a monorepo checkout** (spawns the web app's `sync-canon`/`build` scripts); a no-op-friendly standard for CI. |

---

## ⌨️ Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Cmd + \` / `Ctrl + \` | Toggle Equal Dual-Panel Split View |
| `Cmd + B` / `Ctrl + B` | Toggle File Explorer Sidebar |
| `Cmd + S` / `Ctrl + S` | Save active document directly to disk |

---

## 🛡️ Security & Zero-Leak Architecture

When deployed as a public demo or shared instance, `mdNinja` guarantees that no visitor's credentials or private repository data can ever be accessed by another visitor:

1. OAuth tokens are exchanged ephemerally in `/api/auth/callback/github`.
2. The payload is transferred via `window.opener.postMessage` directly into that visitor's private browser `localStorage`.
3. Zero tokens or private repositories are stored in server memory, cache, or database.

See [ADR 0004](mdninja/decisions/0004-zero-leak-multi-user-isolation.md) for full architectural details.
